questions.stem: Explain when a fixed-effect model is appropriate in a meta-analysis.

answer.exemplar: A fixed-effect model is appropriate when studies are clinically and methodologically similar and heterogeneity is low, so a single common effect is plausible.

questions.explanation: Fixed-effect suits similar studies with low heterogeneity. High heterogeneity favours random-effects.

questions.subject: RESEARCH_METHODS
questions.topic: What a random-effects model adds
questions.stem: A random-effects model reports tau-squared 0.16. What is the standard deviation of true effects?
questions.explanation: Standard deviation is the square root of 0.16, which is 0.4. Tau-squared is the between-study variance.
questions.hint: Take the square root of tau-squared.

questions.subject: RESEARCH_METHODS
questions.topic: Measuring between-study heterogeneity

stimulus.body: A meta-analysis reports I-squared 60% and tau-squared 0.05. A colleague interprets I-squared as the absolute between-study variance.

questions.stem: What is the error in the colleague's interpretation?

options.text: Tau-squared is a proportion, not a variance.
I-squared is a proportion, not an absolute variance.

questions.explanation: I-squared is a proportion of total variance, while tau-squared is the absolute between-study variance. The colleague confuses the two.

questions.topic: What a review protocol commits to in advance
questions.stem: If a review team changes its eligibility criteria after seeing results, what should happen?

options.text: The change must be reported as an amendment.

questions.explanation: Post-hoc changes must be reported as amendments. This preserves transparency about deviations from protocol.

questions.topic: Boolean structure of a search string
questions.learningObjective: Apply parentheses to structure a search
questions.stem: Why are parentheses used in a Boolean search string?

options.text: To group terms so AND/OR apply correctly.

questions.explanation: Parentheses group terms, ensuring AND and OR combine in the intended order. Without them, results may differ.

questions.topic: Operationalising an inclusion criterion
questions.learningObjective: Identify a screening aid from operationalisation
questions.stem: A well-operationalised criterion is turned into a checklist with yes/no questions. What is the main benefit?

options.text: It removes the need for two screeners.

questions.explanation: A checklist helps screeners apply criteria consistently. It does not remove the need for dual screening.

questions.subject: RESEARCH_METHODS
questions.topic: Recording the reason a full text was excluded
questions.learningObjective: Count exclusion reasons in a flow
questions.stem: Explain why recording the reason for each full-text exclusion matters for a review.

answer.exemplar: Recording each exclusion reason creates an auditable trail, lets readers judge whether exclusions were appropriate, and supports PRISMA-compliant reporting.

questions.explanation: Recording reasons supports auditability and PRISMA compliance. It helps readers assess exclusion decisions.
